conceptZh: 窗：穴字頭加囪，牆上透光通風的洞。
object: a barrel-shaped toy pirate with an uncooperative parrot, and a sky-blue toy window with swinging shutters
morph: the pirate proudly builds a silly wrong round porthole, the parrot shakes its head, he shrugs and snaps it into 窗
creativeAngle: 海盜先蓋出圓圓的船窗，鸚鵡搖頭，他聳聳肩一秒修成方方的窗。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 窗 (window), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a barrel-shaped toy pirate with an uncooperative parrot, and a sky-blue toy window with swinging shutters. Sunny lemon-yellow backdrop; the glyph is sky-blue with white highlights and a navy edge. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a barrel-bodied toy pirate rolls in lugging a tiny toolbox, a grumpy red parrot perched on his hat. The voice says the first 窗 as he hammers a blue roof-like cover stroke up at the top. 1.5-3.0s: he steps back and presents a lopsided round porthole made of the blue strokes, bowing proudly; the parrot slowly shakes its head and covers its eyes with a wing. The voice says the second 窗 as the pirate's eyes pop in a double-take. 3.0-4.5s: he shrugs, tugs two pegs, and the whole round shape squares up with a bounce into the correct 窗 at 70% of frame height; the parrot flaps in mock applause. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 窗戶 (ㄔㄨㄤ ㄏㄨˋ) as two toy shutters swing open beside the glyph and the parrot pokes its head through one. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still; the parrot waves a wing from the shutter while the pirate tips his hat. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 窗、窗、窗戶 (ㄔㄨㄤ、ㄔㄨㄤ、ㄔㄨㄤ ㄏㄨˋ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, and stop; no other speech, subtitles or loud music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 窗 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 玩具海盜想在積木小隊砌好的實心牆上開一扇窗看海，雙方抓住綁在牆中央的彈力繩拔河，鸚鵡偏偏降落在繩子正中間，繩子「啪」地一彈，兩邊都摔個屁股蹲，積木牆炸開後磚塊在空中落下疊成「窗」字。
object: a solid wall of deep sea-blue interlocking toy bricks with a stretchy rope tied around its centre brick
morph: the tug-of-war rope snaps, the brick wall bursts, and the scattered bricks tumble and click together in mid-air into the glyph 窗: the top bricks settle as the 穴 roof, the lower bricks lock into the 囪 window-box
creativeAngle: 上一版是安靜的窗板打開，沒有大動作；這版改成完整的拔河鬧劇：海盜要開窗、積木小隊死守牆，鸚鵡在最糟的時機壓垮繩子，繩子彈開的撞擊把牆炸成筆畫，「窗戶」一詞由海盜從殘留的小積木窗框探頭看海來演出，動作、字義、口語三者同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 窗 (window), correctly formed, built from deep sea-blue toy bricks on a pale sand-yellow backdrop, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Cast: a barrel-shaped toy pirate with a wooden peg leg and a stubborn red parrot, versus a squad of deep sea-blue interlocking building bricks with tiny cartoon eyes. Only these things are on screen; nothing busy behind.

0.0–1.5s: The brick squad has just stacked itself into a solid, windowless wall on the right. The pirate waddles in from the left, presses his spyglass against the wall, sees nothing, and stamps his peg leg: he wants a window to see the sea. He points at the wall's centre brick and grabs the end of a stretchy blue rope tied around it. The voice says the first 窗 as he digs in his heels. Behind the wall, the brick squad grabs the other rope end and shakes its heads NO.

1.5–3.5s: TUG-OF-WAR. Pirate leans back, peg leg skidding, round belly straining, face going red; the bricks stack into a tower for leverage and lean the other way. The parrot flatly refuses to help, hovers, then lands squarely on the middle of the rope, sagging it to the floor. The pirate yells silently; the parrot shrugs its wings and hops onto his nose, covering his eyes.

3.5–4.5s: One frozen beat: the rope stretches thin as spaghetti and hums. TWANG! It lets go. Pirate rockets backward and lands on his bottom with a cartoon squash; the brick squad flies the other way and lands in a dazed heap. The wall bursts: bricks tumble through the air and click together as they land, top bricks settling into the 穴 roof of the glyph, lower bricks locking into the 囪 window-box below. The voice says the second 窗 exactly as the last brick snaps into place and the finished 窗 bounces once and stands still, centered at 70% of frame height.

4.5–5.5s: The voice says 窗戶 (ㄔㄨㄤ ㄏㄨˋ) as the pirate sits up at the bottom-left corner, finds a small leftover square brick window frame in front of him, pokes his head and spyglass through it, and at last sees a tiny toy wave bobbing past outside. The parrot lands on the spyglass tip and bends it down.

5.5–8.0s: Final hold. The glyph 窗 stays perfectly still, sharp and fully readable. Away from the strokes, the pirate rubs his bottom with a dizzy grin and tips his hat; the brick heap at bottom-right wobbles, stacks itself into a tiny salute, and topples again; the parrot preens, smug.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 窗、窗、窗戶 (ㄔㄨㄤ、ㄔㄨㄤ、ㄔㄨㄤ ㄏㄨˋ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop; no other speech. Soft cartoon stretch, twang and bonk sounds, no loud startling noises, no music louder than the voice. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 窗 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys.
